settings.editor:
Smile Community Centre serves children from the Soweto–Kayole community in Nairobi. This view of Soweto shows the neighbourhood where children come from and the community at the heart of our work.

Your support helps us provide care, meals and opportunities to learn, while respecting each child’s dignity and connection to their community.
Four programmes, one purpose: care, learning and opportunity for every child in our home and community.
Help children stay in school with support for fees, books, uniforms and learning materials.
Support nutritious daily meals for children in our home and community feeding when resources allow.
Support counselling, referrals and practical assistance for affected children and families, with dignity and care.
Give children opportunities to play, build teamwork and develop their talents through football, basketball and activities.

Our children need nutritious meals every day.

We also organise feeding support for vulnerable children and community members in Soweto, Kayole and nearby areas when donations make it possible.

seo_desc: Since 2009 Smile Community Centre has grown from one woman's commitment into a children's home in Soweto, Kayole, Nairobi. Our story, mission and milestones.

settings.editor: Since 2009, Smile has grown from one woman’s commitment to her neighbours into a children’s home serving orphaned and vulnerable children in Soweto, Kayole.

After recovering from a serious spinal injury, our founder, Margret Nekesa Khaemba, a mother of three, committed herself to serving God through community work. She began by counselling women, teaching home-based care, helping children with food and linking families to schools and health facilities in Kayole and Soweto.

In 2009 she registered the Smile self-help group, which trained women and youth to make beadwork, detergents and food products. Part of the proceeds helped families and bought food for street children.

Her work with street children and orphaned and vulnerable children showed the need for something more formal. In 2016 the group was registered with the Ministry of Labour, Social Security and Services as a Community Based Organisation.

html:
About us

About Smile Community Centre

Since 2009, Smile has grown from one woman’s commitment to her neighbours into a children’s home serving orphaned and vulnerable children in Soweto, Kayole.

Our story

How Smile began

After recovering from a serious spinal injury, our founder, Margret Nekesa Khaemba, a mother of three, committed herself to serving God through community work. She began by counselling women, teaching home-based care, helping children with food and linking families to schools and health facilities in Kayole and Soweto.

In 2009 she registered the Smile self-help group, which trained women and youth to make beadwork, detergents and food products. Part of the proceeds helped families and bought food for street children.

Her work with street children and orphaned and vulnerable children showed the need for something more formal. In 2016 the group was registered with the Ministry of Labour, Social Security and Services as a Community Based Organisation.

Meet our founder

Milestones

From an iron-sheet room to a safer home

  1. Margret’s own homeChildren referred by local police, with nowhere else to go, first lived with Margret’s family, who shared everything they had.
  2. An iron-sheet structure near SabasabaA rented room next to PCEA Kayole church, with no water or electricity. Children studied by kerosene lamp, and when heavy rain came through the roof they returned to Margret’s house.
  3. A reclaimed plot near Steppa Stage, SowetoWith well-wishers’ help, a former dump site was rehabilitated. Lift the Children supported improvements. The site later flooded and was no longer safe.
  4. Our current home at Mzesa, SowetoWith support from individual well-wishers and Thrive Kenya, the centre moved to a rented building at Mzesa.

Our purpose

Mission

To promote self-reliance, education and wellbeing of orphaned and vulnerable children, women and youth in the informal settlements.

Our hope

Vision

To see a community free from illiteracy, lack of sustainable income and poor health.

Our community

Why we work in Soweto and Kayole

Nairobi is a growing city, but many families in its informal settlements live with poverty, poor housing, limited schooling and unreliable income. HIV/AIDS has left many children without parents. Children who lose family support can end up on the streets.

We work with children’s officers, chiefs, police and social workers so that children in danger can be received safely, cared for and, where possible, reunited with capable family members, in line with Kenya’s care reform.

Our goals

Looking ahead

Our dream

We hope to have enough space to care for more children comfortably, and in the long term to open a community school and a health facility for the centre. These are future goals that depend on sustainable support.

title: Our Founder
seo_title: Our Founder Margret Nekesa | Smile Community Centre
seo_desc: Meet Margret Nekesa, who founded Smile Community Centre in Kayole, Nairobi, and turned her own hardship into a safe home for orphaned and vulnerable children.

settings.title: Margret Nekesa: leading with faith and a smile

settings.editor: Margret’s own life shaped her determination to give children a safe and hopeful start.

Margret grew up the eldest daughter in her family. When her parents separated, she and her sisters were sent to their grandfather’s farm, where they herded cattle and she struggled to stay in school. She bought her first pair of shoes after primary school.

As an adult she worked as a tea picker. A severe spinal condition left her bedridden from 1996 to 2003, caring for three children from a single room. Her own children often went out looking for food and came home with other street children. Margret prayed that she would walk again so that she could help them.

Margret recovered and began serving her community. Through her relationships with local head teachers she enrolled children in school, sometimes before fees could be paid. The home began in her own house, where her family shared clothes and bedding with children who had nowhere else to go.

From there the centre moved to an iron-sheet structure, then to a reclaimed dump site that later flooded, and finally to its current rented building at Mzesa, Soweto, through fundraising with family and friends of Smile.

Today Margret’s three children support her through their own networks to keep improving the centre. She believes that a simple smile, joined with practical care, can change a child’s world.

title: Our Goals
seo_title: Mission, Vision and Objectives | Smile Community Centre
seo_desc: Our mission: self-reliance, education and wellbeing for orphaned and vulnerable children, women and youth in Nairobi's informal settlements. Our ten objectives.

settings.editor: What we work towards today, and what we hope to achieve with sustainable support.

html:
Our goals

Mission, vision and objectives

What we work towards today, and what we hope to achieve with sustainable support.

Mission

To promote self-reliance, education and wellbeing of orphaned and vulnerable children, women and youth in the informal settlements.

Vision

To see a community free from illiteracy, lack of sustainable income and poor health.

Our objectives

  • Provide food, shelter and education for orphaned and vulnerable children.
  • Raise awareness of HIV/AIDS, which has left many children orphaned, and fight stigma and discrimination.
  • Offer training in hygiene, environmental management, and skills and technical training.
  • Offer counselling, medical referral, and food and nutrition support.
  • Help young people and the wider community understand good nutrition and health through home-based care and feeding programmes.
  • Promote awareness of preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission, and maternal, newborn and child health among young women.
  • Encourage exchange between Smile and local, national and international organisations to build capacity and share ideas and culture.
  • Provide psychological support through counselling for teenagers, youth and women.
  • Develop talent through sports and games.
  • Advocate for human rights and the right to live positively.

Long-term goals

Expanding our reach

When sustainable donor funding allows, Smile hopes to mobilise more communities across Kenya by opening further rescue centres for orphaned and vulnerable children, and to build a community school and health facility. These are aspirations, not current services.

title: Education Programme
seo_title: Sponsor a Child's Education in Kenya | Smile Nairobi
seo_desc: Help a child in Kayole, Nairobi stay in school. Support school fees, uniforms, books and mentoring through Smile Community Centre's education programme.

settings.editor: Every child in our care goes to school. We help them stay there.

In Nairobi’s informal settlements, poverty and difficult living conditions make it hard for children to learn. Some children are orphaned, and others are displaced from home by family conflict.

Smile hosts and educates orphaned and vulnerable children from Kayole and Soweto. We began in an iron-sheet room without electricity, where children studied at night by kerosene lamp. Today, thanks to well-wishers, we offer full-time educational support to the children who live in our home.

settings.title: From our first classroom to university

settings.editor:
Two of the first teenagers we rescued completed secondary school and qualified for university, one to study industrial chemistry and the other metrology. Former residents continue their studies through scholarships, well-wishers and part-time work.

Our core support covers primary and secondary education. We are looking for partners to help young people make the move into college, technical training and work.

html:

Education lights the way

Why education matters here

In Nairobi’s informal settlements, poverty and difficult living conditions make it hard for children to learn. Some children are orphaned, and others are displaced from home by family conflict.

Smile hosts and educates orphaned and vulnerable children from Kayole and Soweto. We began in an iron-sheet room without electricity, where children studied at night by kerosene lamp. Today, thanks to well-wishers, we offer full-time educational support to the children who live in our home.

title: Feeding Programme
seo_title: Feeding Programme for Children in Nairobi | Smile
seo_desc: Daily meals and clean water for orphaned and vulnerable children in Soweto, Kayole, Nairobi. See how food and water donations support Smile's feeding programme.

settings.title: No child should learn or grow on an empty stomach

settings.editor: We feed the children in our home every day and run a community feeding programme in Soweto and Kayole.

Malnutrition is common among children in informal settlements and affects both physical growth and brain development. Many families struggle to afford a single meal a day.

Our feeding programme runs seasonally with the support of well-wishers. It mainly reaches women and children who cannot afford a meal, and it involves other children’s homes in Kayole, Donholm and Soweto. When enough food is donated, families come to our office for a meal and receive cereals or flour to take home.
We would like to run the feeding programme regularly rather than seasonally, and to reach neighbouring areas such as Sabasaba, Kayole One and Matopeni. Doing so depends on steady support.

title: Child Care and Shelter
seo_title: Child Care and Shelter in Nairobi | Smile Children's Home
seo_desc: A safe home, care and protection for orphaned and vulnerable children in Soweto, Kayole, Nairobi, working with children's officers and Kenya's care reform.

settings.title: A safe place to sleep, eat, learn and heal

settings.editor: We receive children who have no safe place to stay and give them a stable, caring home.

Police officers, children’s officers, local chiefs and community social workers contact us when a child has nowhere safe to go. We shelter children only with the authorisation documents required from the police, the court or the children’s office.

Each child receives immediate shelter, daily meals, clothing and medical care, and is enrolled in school. We continue supporting them with guidance, education and a stable environment.

settings.title: Family first, where it is safe

settings.editor:
In line with the Government of Kenya’s care reform, we take part in reintegrating children with capable family members in their communities. This lets us focus on children who urgently need rescue.

We do not arrange adoptions. Anyone wishing to adopt should contact their nearest children’s office or a certified adoption agency, as required by Kenyan law.

seo_desc: Medical care, hygiene, nutrition and counselling for the children at Smile Community Centre in Kayole, Nairobi. Learn how you can help.

settings.editor: Medical care, counselling and referrals for children in our home and families in our community.

Some children arrive needing urgent treatment. We make sure each child receives medical care and is linked to health facilities. Volunteer doctors have also supported our children.

Clean water is a constant challenge in Soweto. Water arrives about once a week and barely fills our 1,500-litre and 3,000-litre tanks, which we rely on for drinking, cooking and hygiene.

HIV/AIDS continues to affect many families in sub-Saharan Africa, and women and children often carry the greatest burden. In Nairobi’s informal settlements, many affected women and children are displaced and fear stigma and discrimination. The red ribbon in our logo represents our solidarity with them.

  • Children orphaned by HIV/AIDS: counselling, shelter, education, food, and referrals for group therapy and medical care.
  • Women affected by abuse: referrals for counselling and any help within our reach. We do not provide shelter for adults.

title: Volunteer With Us
seo_title: Volunteer at a Children's Home in Kenya | Smile, Nairobi
seo_desc: Volunteer with children in Nairobi: teaching, mentoring, sports, counselling and daily care at Smile Community Centre, Kayole. Local and overseas volunteers.

settings.editor: We welcome volunteers who want to promote positive growth in our community.
Whether you can give a morning or a few months, there is a place for your skills at Smile.

Children’s safety comes first. Every volunteer signs a volunteer agreement and is expected to:

  • Follow staff guidance at all times and never be alone with a child out of sight of staff.
  • Never photograph, film or post about children without the centre’s permission, and never share children’s names, locations or stories online.
  • Never give children personal contact details or contact them outside the centre.
  • Treat every child and community member with dignity and respect.
  • Report any concern about a child’s safety to the centre’s management immediately.

We may ask for references or a police clearance certificate as part of our approval process. We will explain how to share these securely. Please do not send identity documents through the form below.
Volunteers from overseas are welcome. Here is what to expect before you apply.

html:
Volunteer with us

Share your time and skills

We welcome volunteers who want to promote positive growth in our community.

[smile_volunteer_notice]

Ways to volunteer

  • Teaching and tutoring
  • Mentoring young people

  • Organising youth activities and community awareness events with our staff
  • Proposal writing and record keeping
  • Online and community fundraising
  • Sports coaching

If you have other ideas for Smile, please tell us.

What we look for

  • Patience, and care for people with special needs
  • Basic knowledge of HIV/AIDS, with zero discrimination towards anyone affected
  • A real interest in helping people in need

Safeguarding and conduct

Children’s safety comes first. Every volunteer signs a volunteer agreement and is expected to:

  • Follow staff guidance at all times and never be alone with a child out of sight of staff.
  • Never photograph, film or post about children without the centre’s permission, and never share children’s names, locations or stories online.
  • Never give children personal contact details or contact them outside the centre.
  • Treat every child and community member with dignity and respect.
  • Report any concern about a child’s safety to the centre’s management immediately.

We may ask for references or a police clearance certificate as part of our approval process. We will explain how to share these securely. Please do not send identity documents through the form below.

International volunteers

Volunteers from overseas are welcome. All volunteer work is unpaid. International volunteers pay a one-time administration fee of US$165 and cover their own living costs, including airport transfers, accommodation and meals. Accommodation can be arranged with a secure local host family or at a nearby hotel or hostel, usually 1 to 5 km from the centre. The project hosts between one and four volunteers a month.

Bring a mosquito net, a torch, toiletries, a first-aid kit, sun cream and durable shoes. All of these can also be bought in Nairobi.

tabs.tab_title: How many children do you care for?

tabs.tab_title: Where do the children come from?
tabs.tab_content: Most children who are abandoned come to us through the police, the children’s office or the local chief’s office, who work with us to identify children in urgent need of rescue. html:
FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Answers to common questions about our home, our children and how to help.

How many children do you care for?

We provide full-time care to orphaned, abandoned and vulnerable children in our home, and our outreach feeding programme benefits more than 300 children. We hope to care for more children once we have more space and resources.

How old are the children?

Our children range from very young children to teenagers in secondary school.

Where do the children come from?

Most children who are abandoned come to us through the police, the children’s office or the local chief’s office, who work with us to identify children in urgent need of rescue. Some are identified by community social workers. We also take part in reuniting children with capable family members, in line with Kenya’s care reform.

Do you have an outreach programme?

Yes. Our outreach feeding programme supports more than 300 children in Soweto and Kayole. We also provide food support to widows and single parents who come to the centre. We welcome partners for this programme.

Do you sell donated clothes?

No. Extra donations are given to people in need during our outreach programmes, and some clothes go to people in need in rural Kenya.

Can I adopt a child from Smile?

We do not offer children for adoption. Please visit your nearest children’s office or a certified adoption agency for guidance under Kenyan law.

Do you support children after secondary school?

Our core educational support covers primary and secondary school. Some former residents are at university through scholarships and help from well-wishers, and we work with technical institutions to help others gain skills for work. We are looking for partners to support this transition.

How can I donate by M-Pesa?

Go to Lipa na M-Pesa, choose Pay Bill and enter business number [smile_setting key="mpesa_paybill"] and account number [smile_setting key="mpesa_account"]. See the Donate page for full steps.

Yes, by arrangement. Please call or WhatsApp us, or use the visit request form on our Contact page.

title: Privacy Policy

seo_desc: How Smile Community Centre collects, uses and protects personal information on this website.

settings.editor: Last updated: October 2026. This draft needs to be reviewed by the centre before launch.

Who we are

Smile Community Centre Children’s Home ("Smile", "we") is a Community Based Organisation in Soweto, Kayole, Nairobi, Kenya. Contact: [smile_setting key="email"], [smile_setting key="postal_address"].

What we collect

  • Forms: when you use our contact, visit, volunteer, partnership, donation or removal request forms, we collect what you enter, such as your name, email, phone number and message.
  • Donations: M-Pesa and bank payments are processed by Safaricom and your bank, not by this website. We never see or store your PIN or card details. If you send us a payment reference, we use it only to confirm your gift.
  • Technical data: our hosting provider keeps standard server logs. Our forms use a one-way coded version of your IP address to limit spam; we do not store your IP address with your message.
  • Cookies: this website uses only the cookies WordPress needs to work. We do not use advertising cookies. If we add analytics in future, we will update this policy.
  • Embedded content: our Contact page shows a Google Map, and some pages may show content from Instagram or Facebook. These services may collect data under their own policies.

How we use it

We use your information only to respond to you, to arrange visits, volunteering or partnerships, and to confirm donations. We do not sell or rent your information.

Who can see it

Messages are stored securely in our website’s admin area and sent by email to authorised Smile staff. Only staff with permission can view them.

How long we keep it

Form messages are deleted automatically after 12 months unless we need them for an ongoing volunteer, partnership or legal matter.

Your rights

Under Kenya’s Data Protection Act, 2019, you can ask to see, correct or delete the information we hold about you, or object to how we use it. Email us at [smile_setting key="email"] and we will respond promptly.

Children’s privacy

We do not knowingly collect information from children through this website. We protect the identities of the children in our care as described in our Safeguarding statement.
